text: なかには　きのみが　はいってるぜ　やくに　たつ　きのみも　はいって　いるから　だいじに　つかって　くれよ！

structure.jp: なかには　きのみが　はいってるぜ
やくに　たつ　きのみも　はいって　いるから
structure.en: useful Berries are in there too, so

structure.jp: だいじに　つかって　くれよ！

patterns.name: 〜てくれ
patterns.explanation: くれ after a て-form verb is a blunt, manly way of asking someone to do something for you. つかって　くれ = 'use them, will you'.

patterns.name: 〜から (reason)
patterns.span: はいって　いるから
patterns.explanation: から after a finished statement gives it as the reason for what comes next, like 'so'. はいって　いるから = 'they are in there, so'.

patterns.name: 〜ている
patterns.explanation: ている after a verb can show a state that stays after something happened; てる is the casual short form. The ぜ after it is a rough, manly ending. はいってる = 'are inside'.
